data.why: The repo ships real instrument-output fixtures for all four supported parsers (Qubit, TapeStation, Tecan Spark, BMG CLARIOstar) including edge cases like an out-of-range/N-A concentration, so these are handed to the browser as-is instead of synthesizing new ones; seed/supabase.py is a small in-memory stand-in for the pip supabase client (the app's own directory is first on sys.path, so this shadows the real package) and seed/.env sets dummy SUPABASE_URL/KEY so every create_client() call succeeds and the app's deck-configuration, pipeline-run and run-data-upload CRUD calls work entirely offline instead of raising SupabaseException or hanging on unreachable network calls.

goals: Browse the 58-assay library, open an assay's dossier and read its robot steps, deck layout, acceptance criteria and regulatory references
Compare two or three assays side-by-side on robot time and throughput
Use the five-question Experiment Wizard to get a recommended assay panel with a robot-time estimate and reagent list
Run a pipeline for a chosen assay (simulated) and hand off the completed run to Upload Run Data
Upload a real instrument output file (e.g. test_qubit.csv) and review the pass/fail verdict against the assay's structured acceptance criteria
Design or edit a deck layout in the Deck Designer and preview the generated PyLabRobot-style setup code

review.summary: The tree is accurate and well evidenced for what it covers: browsing and reading the library, comparing assays, the four-step setup wizard with code export, the simulated run, and checking instrument files against acceptance criteria. Its labels are clean. But the server hang meant it missed two of the six stated goals (Experiment Wizard, Deck Designer), and it wrongly says the dossier has no export, so it needs a targeted re-run and the listed corrections before filing.
